![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/0405639a97f249bbcc4dc18a7eae5b4df24aefb4b4680b569365b3d841c15e6b.png)

   

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $y$-axis and the lines $x=\dfrac{y}2$ and $x=y-2$, as shown above. The mass density function of the plate is $\lambda(x,y) =\dfrac y8.$ Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=2.$
e-12485.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
I_l = \iint\limits_D \lambda (x,y) [r(x,y)]^2 \:\textrm{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \:\: 2x \leq y \leq x+2 \right\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/69dcf02cc1883f2b04f81bd6dd486bbe24fedbb813db5778ae3b33ed1fb42e90.png)

     

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y) = |x - 2|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{2x}^{x+2}(\frac{y}{8})|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{2x}^{x+2}(\frac{y}{8})(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(x-2)^{2}{\int }_{2x}^{x+2}\frac{y}{8}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(x-2)^{2}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{16}]}_{2x}^{x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}(x-2)^{2}((x+2)^{2}-(2x)^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4)(4+4x-3{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}(16-24{x}^{2}+16{x}^{3}-3{x}^{4})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{[16x-8{x}^{3}+4{x}^{4}-\frac{3{x}^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}(32-64+64-\frac{96}{5})-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{16}(\frac{64}{5}) \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 1}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=x+y-1$ Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $x=2.$
after.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-2|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x+y-1)|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-2+y+1)(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-2)^{3}+(y+1)(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{[y(x-2)^{3}+\frac{1}{2}(y+1)^{2}(x-2)^{2}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}(x-2)^{3}+\frac{3}{2}(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{(x-2)^{4}}{4}+\frac{(x-2)^{3}}{2}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2})-(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=-2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-(-2)|=|x+2|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y-x)|x+2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y-x)(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}y(x+2)^{2}-x(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}(x+2)^{2}-xy(x+2)^{2}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{1}(3-2x)(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{1}(-2{x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}+4x+12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{-{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{5{x}^{3}}{3}+2{x}^{2}+12x]}_{-2}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{5}{3}+2+12)-(-8+\frac{40}{3}+8-24)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((14-\frac{13}{6})-(-24+\frac{40}{3})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{135}{6}) \\  & =\frac{45}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 1,\,\,1\le y\le 2}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=y-x.$ Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $x=-2.$
content.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=-2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-(-2)|=|x+2|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y-x)|x+2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y-x)(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}y(x+2)^{2}-x(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}(x+2)^{2}-xy(x+2)^{2}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{1}(3-2x)(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{1}(-2{x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}+4x+12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{-{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{5{x}^{3}}{3}+2{x}^{2}+12x]}_{-2}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{5}{3}+2+12)-(-8+\frac{40}{3}+8-24)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((14-\frac{13}{6})-(-24+\frac{40}{3})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{135}{6}) \\  & =\frac{45}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
